sections.heading: C — Getting your Washington license
sections.markdown:
## C — Getting your Washington license

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A18
Every Washington license, permit and ID card carries a personal Washington number that often starts with the letters WDL. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A18
License Express is the secure DOL website, and each new driver must open an account in their own name because services cannot be obtained through someone else's account. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A19
You count as a Washington resident when any single listed condition applies, such as keeping a home here for personal use, being registered to vote here, filing taxes with a Washington address, or receiving state public assistance. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A20
A new resident aged 18 or older who is licensed in another state has 30 days to get a Washington driver license. [A20]
Why it matters: a common mix-up is assuming an out-of-state license is good here indefinitely.
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A20
If a new resident's out-of-state license has expired, they must pass both the knowledge exam and the skills exam before Washington will license them. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A20
A new resident under 18 with another state's license applies for a Washington Intermediate Driver License, and DOL must approve their driver education and confirm at least 6 months of instruction-permit time. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A24
REAL ID is a law rather than a card, and an enhanced license or ID is one of several options that satisfy it; a standard license will no longer be accepted at airport security, border crossings or secure federal buildings. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A25
You must already have a WDL number before you apply for an instruction permit. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A25
When you enroll in driver training you may apply for a permit as young as 15, online or at an office, from 1 to 10 days before the course starts. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A25
Without driver training you may take the knowledge exam after turning 15½ and get the permit once you pass, but the skills exam and license must wait until you are 18. [A25]
Why it matters: the two permit ages are a classic confusable pair, the younger age belongs to the training-course path.
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A25
An instruction permit is valid for 1 year and can be renewed for a fee, while a passing knowledge exam score stays valid for 2 years. [A25]
Why it matters: wait too long for the skills exam and you may have to retake the knowledge exam.
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A26
To get a first license at 16 or 17 you must have held the permit for at least 6 months, be at least 16, live in Washington, and complete a traffic safety course at an approved driver training school. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A26
A traffic safety course finished in another state counts only if it meets Washington's minimum of 30 classroom hours and 6 behind-the-wheel hours. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A26
A teen applicant must log at least 40 hours of daytime and 10 hours of nighttime driving beside a licensed driver with 3 or more years of experience, attested by a parent, guardian or responsible adult. [A26]
Why it matters: the supervising driver's experience requirement differs for adults, see the adult permit route.
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A26
A teen applicant must go 6 months with no traffic violations or convictions before applying, and must have no alcohol or drug offenses while driving on the permit. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A26
For an in-person teen application a parent or guardian signs an authorization form certifying at least 50 hours of driving experience and no traffic infractions or violations during the previous 6 months. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A27
Once a teen passes each exam, the driver training school has 24 hours to record the scores in the DOL system. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A27
An in-person applicant leaves the office with a temporary license good for 45 days, and the official card arrives later by mail. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A27
When a teen completes the license online, the printed receipt is the temporary license, but it carries no photo and so cannot serve as identification. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A28
An adult first-time applicant has four routes: transfer another state's license, pass both exams, pass the knowledge exam and practice on a permit beside a licensed driver with 5 or more years of experience before the skills exam, or use an exam waiver to get a permit and finish a training course before both exams. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A28
Drivers aged 16 and 17 move through two restricted phases, first the instruction permit and then the intermediate driver license, before they hold an unrestricted license. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A28
In the first 6 months of an intermediate license you may not carry any passenger under age 20 unless that person is an immediate family member. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A28
After those first 6 months, and until you turn 18 or reach one year on the license, whichever is first, you may carry no more than 3 passengers under age 20 who are not immediate family. [A28]
Why it matters: learners often swap the zero-passenger phase and the limited-passenger phase.
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec01-F24 | anchor: A28
An intermediate driver may not drive from 1 a.m. to 5 a.m. unless a parent, guardian or licensed driver aged at least 25 rides along, and this night limit ends after one year of safe driving. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec01-F25 | anchor: A29
Intermediate license holders may not use a cell phone or wireless device while driving, even hands-free, except to report an emergency. [A29]
Why it matters: a frequent wrong answer is that hands-free use is allowed for new drivers.
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec01-F26 | anchor: A29
For an intermediate driver, a first violation or at-fault collision keeps the current restrictions until age 18, a second brings a 6-month suspension or suspension until 18 if that comes sooner, and a third suspends the license until 18. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec01-F27 | anchor: A29
An intermediate driver may drive at any hour with passengers when the trip is for agricultural purposes, or after one year with no crash and no traffic offense. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec01-F28 | anchor: A29
Intermediate restrictions drop away automatically at 18, so no new license is required then, and an updated card can wait until renewal. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec01-F29 | anchor: A29
An agricultural permit lets a driver under 18 drive within a set area for farm work, and the juvenile agricultural permit has no minimum age. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec01-F30 | anchor: A30
An agricultural permit never substitutes for an instruction permit and does not waive any requirement for a first Washington license, including practice driving. [A30]
Source: [A30 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec01-F31 | anchor: A30
DOL mails an early warning letter to drivers aged 18 to 21 after their first moving violation, because a driver's crash risk doubles after that first violation. [A30]
Source: [A30 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec01-F32 | anchor: A30
DOL screens your vision before issuing a license, and if you need glasses or contacts that requirement is noted on the license, so wear them every time you drive. [A30]
Source: [A30 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec01-F33 | anchor: A31
Driving a motorcycle or a commercial motor vehicle requires an extra endorsement added to your personal driver license. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0031]

Glossary: WDL number — your personal Washington licensing number [A18]. Intermediate driver license — the restricted teen license between the permit and the full license [A28]. Endorsement — an add-on that authorizes a special vehicle type [A31].
Memory aid: for the intermediate license think "zero, then few, then free" — no young passengers, then a small number, then no limit once restrictions lift. [A28]
